subtitle: From Kashmir’s Snow to Kalyani’s Gold: A Poet Walks an India of Kings and Manuscripts

panels.shot: wide tracking shot across a painted map of India, morphing into a lone traveler on a mountain pass
panels.action: Bilhana strides along a narrow Himalayan path, manuscripts at his waist, snow peaks behind and a hazy plains horizon ahead, as if he himself is crossing a giant map of India.

dialogue.text: In the age of Vikramaditya VI, Bilhana of Kashmir walked across India with only verses and hope, and turned a southern king into an epic hero forever.

i18n.hi: विक्रमादित्य षष्ठ के दौर में, कश्मीर का बिल्हण केवल श्लोकों और उम्मीद के साथ पूरे भारत में चला, और एक दक्षिणी राजा को सदियों का महायोद्धा बना दिया।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Bilhana writing by lamplight
panels.action: Young Bilhana sits in a Kashmiri house, reed pen poised over palm-leaf, lamplight on his focused face, snow-lit roofs visible through a lattice window.

dialogue.text: Our story begins in Kashmir, where Bilhana first learned that gods, kings and love could all be caught in Sanskrit verse, though the world around him was already trembling with change.

i18n.hi: कहानी शुरू होती है कश्मीर से, जहाँ बिल्हण ने पहली बार देखा कि देवता, राजा और प्रेम सब संस्कृत में बाँध दिए जा सकते हैं, जबकि उसके चारों ओर दुनिया बदलती हुई काँप रही थी।

panels.shot: medium shot, side profile, with distant temple and palace
panels.action: Bilhana stands at a height, looking down at Srinagar’s river, temples and wooden houses, a small bundle of manuscripts in his hand, clouds heavy above.

dialogue.text: Kalhana’s Rajatarangini remembers Bilhana as one more thread in Kashmir’s tapestry of scholars, before politics and patronage pushed many learned men to seek fortunes far from home.

i18n.hi: कल्हण की राजतरंगिणी में बिल्हण कश्मीर की विद्वान चादर का एक और धागा है, सत्ता और सरपरस्तों के खेल से पहले, जब कई पंडित दूर-दूर भाग्य खोजने निकल पड़े।

panels.shot: low-angle, Bilhana at a crossroads leaving Kashmir
panels.action: At a rocky mountain pass marked by a small shrine, Bilhana turns his back on Kashmir, stepping onto a dusty path leading south, the valley receding behind him.

dialogue.text: Bilhana’s own Vikramanka-deva-charita tells us that he left Kashmir as a wandering poet, carrying praise and learning like a portable homeland, walking towards the great schools of the plains.

i18n.hi: बिल्हण की विक्रमांक देव-चरित खुद कहती है कि वह कश्मीर से खानाबदोश कवि की तरह निकला, ज्ञान और स्तुति को चलते-फिरते वतन की तरह साथ लेकर, मैदानों के महान विद्यालयों की ओर।

panels.shot: wide shot of riverside ghats at Varanasi
panels.action: Bilhana walks along crowded ghats in Varanasi, ascetics, students and ritual fires around him, as he lifts his eyes to towering temple spires above the Ganga.

dialogue.text: He reached Varanasi, where the Ganga carried debates like foam. Here, seasoned pandits tested him, and Bilhana’s verses first tasted the wider Sanskrit world.

i18n.hi: वह वाराणसी पहुँचा, जहाँ गंगा बहसों को फेन की तरह उछालती थी। यहाँ पुराने पंडितों ने उसे परखा, और बिल्हण के श्लोकों ने पहली बार बड़े संस्कृत संसार का स्वाद चखा।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot in a debating hall
panels.action: Inside a modest hall, Bilhana stands at the center, reciting to seated scholars, while palm-leaf manuscripts lie stacked on a low platform, and an oil lamp flickers.

dialogue.text: In his poem’s closing canto, he recalls scholars who weighed his words as carefully as scripture. Their approval was a passport to the next court, the next chance.

i18n.hi: अंतिम सर्ग में वह उन विद्वानों को याद करता है जो उसके शब्दों को शास्त्र जैसी तौल से जाँचते थे। उनकी स्वीकृति ही अगली सभा, अगले मौक़े का पासपोर्ट थी।

panels.shot: wide, dusty road with passing caravan near Kannauj
panels.action: Bilhana joins a caravan on a broad plain road, bullock carts and riders beside him, distant walls of Kannauj silhouetted against the evening sky.

dialogue.text: From Varanasi he moved through Kannauj and other northern centers, following invisible scholar roads linking monasteries, temples and palaces, where language itself was a currency.

i18n.hi: वाराणसी से वह कन्नौज और दूसरे उत्तरी नगरों से गुज़रा, उन अदृश्य विद्वान-रास्तों पर जो विहारों, मंदिरों और महलों को जोड़ते थे, जहाँ भाषा ही चलन थी।

panels.shot: overhead shot of Bilhana resting under a tree, map etched in dust
panels.action: Bilhana sits under a lone tree, drawing lines with a stick in the dust that suggest the Indian peninsula, his bag of manuscripts resting beside him, the sun harsh overhead.

dialogue.text: By his own telling, his wandering stretched for years. The poem compresses this long hunger into a few shining lines: a scholar walking south, searching for a king worthy of a mahakavya.

i18n.hi: उसके शब्दों से पता चलता है कि यह भटकन बरसों चली। कविता इस लंबी भूख को कुछ चमकती पंक्तियों में दबा देती है: एक विद्वान दक्षिण की ओर चलता, उस राजा की खोज में जो महाकाव्य लायक हो।

panels.shot: dramatic reveal of Deccan landscape approaching Kalyani
panels.action: A sweeping view shows Bilhana cresting a hill to see the Deccan’s rolling plains and a distant fortified city, Kalyani, under a blazing sky.

dialogue.text: At last he reached the Deccan, and Kalyani, capital of the Western Chalukyas, where Vikramaditya VI ruled a court already humming with mathematicians, jurists and poets.

i18n.hi: आख़िर वह दक्खिन और कल्याणी पहुँचा, पश्चिमी चालुक्यों की राजधानी, जहाँ विक्रमादित्य षष्ठ की सभा पहले ही गणितज्ञों, न्यायविदों और कवियों से गूँज रही थी।

panels.shot: interior throne-hall, medium-wide with king implied off-frame
panels.action: Bilhana stands in a grand hall before an unseen royal figure, pillars carved with lotus motifs and warriors, other courtiers watching as he bows with measured dignity.

dialogue.text: Bilhana’s Vikramanka-deva-charita turns this meeting into legend. He presents himself as the wandering poet whose skill convinces Vikramaditya to make him Vidyapati, the lord of learning at court.

i18n.hi: बिल्हण की विक्रमांक देव-चरित इस भेंट को दंतकथा बना देती है। वह खुद को ऐसे फिरते कवि के रूप में दिखाता है, जिसकी कला विक्रमादित्य को उसे विद्यापति, राजसभा के ज्ञान-स्वामी बनाने पर राज़ी कर देती है।

panels.shot: close-up on Bilhana’s face as he recites
panels.action: Bilhana, eyes bright, mouth mid-verse, recites with raised hand, while blurred glimpses of royal ornaments and attentive courtiers ring the frame.

dialogue.text: “O Vikramanka, your name fills my verse as the moon fills the night.”

i18n.hi: “हे विक्रमांक, तुम्हारा नाम मेरी कविता को वैसे भर देता है जैसे चाँद रात को।”

panels.shot: symbolic montage shot with king’s hand bestowing a manuscript
panels.action: A richly adorned hand reaches out, offering a freshly bound palm-leaf manuscript to Bilhana, who receives it with both hands, head lowered, lamps glowing in the background.

dialogue.text: Whether the title came exactly as he says, the poem shows what mattered: a northern scholar absorbed into a southern court, given the task of weaving his king into cosmic story.

i18n.hi: उपाधि सच-सच आई या नहीं, इससे ज़्यादा मायने यह है कि उत्तर का विद्वान दक्षिण की सभा का हिस्सा बना, और उसे अपने राजा को ब्रह्मांडीय कथा में बुनने का काम सौंपा गया।

panels.shot: tableau of Bilhana writing the Vikramanka-deva-charita
panels.action: In a quiet chamber, Bilhana sits cross-legged, palm-leaf spread before him, as an assistant holds an ink pot; outside an open door, the palace courtyard hints at royal life continuing.

dialogue.text: Here he composed the Vikramanka-deva-charita, eighteen cantos of Sanskrit praise that crowned Vikramaditya’s reign with gods, conquests and virtues, and smuggled in his own journey at the end.

i18n.hi: यहीं उसने विक्रमांक देव-चरित रचा, अठारह संस्कृत सर्गों की स्तुति, जिसने विक्रमादित्य के राज को देवताओं, विजयों और गुणों का मुकुट दिया, और अंत में चुपके से उसकी अपनी यात्रा भी टाँक दी।

panels.shot: dynamic montage of imagined battles fading behind Bilhana
panels.action: Bilhana writes while ghostly images of marching armies, distant cities and oceans rise behind him like painted scenes, then fade, leaving only his focused figure.

dialogue.text: The poem claims campaigns in Kanchi, Bengal, even Simhala. Modern historians treat these victories as courtly self-fashioning, not firm record, reading the verses as careful art more than plain report.

i18n.hi: कविता कांची, बंगाल, यहाँ तक कि सिहल तक के अभियानों का दावा करती है। आज के इतिहासकार इन जीतों को दरबारी खुद-की-गढ़ी छवि मानते हैं, पंक्तियों को सधी हुई कला की तरह पढ़ते हैं, सीधे इतिहास की तरह नहीं।

panels.shot: medium shot beside a jurist teaching, law manuscripts visible
panels.action: Bilhana stands near a jurist instructing students over law manuscripts, shelves lined with texts, hinting at the intellectual court world linked to works like the Mitakshara.

dialogue.text: Around such courts, jurists would later craft texts like the Mitakshara. Bilhana’s poem shows that kings sought legitimacy in both law and literature, wrapping their power in learned Sanskrit.

i18n.hi: ऐसी ही सभाओं के आस-पास आगे चलकर मिताक्षरा जैसे न्यायग्रंथ बने। बिल्हण की कविता दिखाती है कि राजा को वैधता कानून में भी चाहिए थी और साहित्य में भी, अपनी शक्ति को संस्कृत विद्वता में लपेटकर।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot of Bilhana reading his own closing canto
panels.action: Seen from behind, Bilhana rereads the final canto of his manuscript, where lines about roads, rivers and cities are visible, his shoulders relaxed, a faint smile on his lips.

dialogue.text: In that last canto, he briefly turns away from his king to speak of himself: the Kashmiri traveler who crossed Varanasi, Kannauj and the Deccan, following rumor of patronage like a distant drum.

i18n.hi: उस आख़िरी सर्ग में वह थोड़ी देर राजा से हटकर खुद पर आता है: वह कश्मीरी यात्री, जिसने वाराणसी, कन्नौज और दक्खिन पार किए, सरपरस्ती की अफ़वाह को दूर के नगाड़े की गूँज की तरह पीछा करते हुए।

panels.shot: high-angle shot of a scribe copying the manuscript
panels.action: A court scribe carefully copies Bilhana’s text onto new palm-leaves, as the original lies open beside him, while courtiers move through the corridor beyond.

dialogue.text: From Kalyani, copies of his mahakavya traveled. Through them, Vikramaditya VI’s name, polished by Bilhana’s art, reached far beyond his actual armies and courts.

i18n.hi: कल्याणी से उसके महाकाव्य की प्रतियाँ निकलीं। उन्हीं से, बिल्हण की चमक से पॉलिश हुआ विक्रमादित्य षष्ठ का नाम, उसकी असल सेनाओं और दरबारों से कहीं दूर तक पहुँच गया।

panels.shot: timeless shot of Bilhana seated among scattered manuscripts from many regions
panels.action: In a symbolic, almost timeless space, Bilhana sits amid scattered manuscripts labelled in faint stylized script as Kashmir, Varanasi, Kannauj, Kalyani, looking up as if hearing distant voices.

dialogue.text: Scholars like Sheldon Pollock and P.N. Kawthekar see his work as part of a cosmopolitan Sanskrit world, where a poet from one region could shape how another king remembered himself.

i18n.hi: शेल्डन पॉलॉक और पी.एन. कावठेकर जैसे विद्वान उसके काम को उस विश्व-संस्कृत जगत का हिस्सा मानते हैं, जहाँ एक प्रांत का कवि किसी दूसरे राजा की यादों की शक्ल बदल सकता था।

panels.shot: slow pull-back from Bilhana’s weathered hands on the manuscript
panels.action: An extreme close-up of Bilhana’s hands resting gently on his closed manuscript, the camera pulling back to reveal the faint outlines of India beyond like a map drawn in light.

dialogue.text: Bilhana shows us that praise can preserve a king and a journey, yet stretch truth into legend; to read his verses is to walk his India, and to weigh every shining line with care.

i18n.hi: बिल्हण हमें दिखाता है कि स्तुति राजा और यात्रा दोनों को बचा सकती है, पर सच को खींचकर कथा भी बना देती है; उसकी पंक्तियाँ पढ़ना मानो उसके भारत में चलना है, और हर चमकते शब्द को तौलकर समझना।

title_i18n.en: Bilhana Crosses India for a King
title_i18n.hi: राजा के लिए बिल्हण ने पार की भारतभूमि
